title: Failsafe policy templates and error classification for cross-language SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define a small set of opinionated, cross-language defaults and developer-friendly templates for retry/backoff behavior, idempotency-key semantics, and streaming resume/deduplication so Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs behave consistently and reduce duplicate side-effects in production.

Goals: Provide safe-by-default policies for mutation vs idempotent calls; an explicit, auditable idempotency key contract; a retryable-error taxonomy that maps HTTP/gRPC errors and internal transient flags to client actions; streaming resume ergonomics (resume tokens, checkpoint cadence, deduplication window); and a lightweight migration path for existing customers.

Non-Goals: This ticket does not change server-side behavior or introduce new server APIs (except recommending consistently-named headers/tokens). It also does not prescribe language-specific APIs beyond surface names (RetryPolicy, IdempotencyScope, StreamResumeManager) and examples that the SDK teams can map idiomatically.

Proposed Defaults (rationale in-line):
- Default policy templates (exported in each SDK):
  - conservative_mutation (safe default for write-like operations that may have side effects): max_attempts=2, initial_backoff_ms=150, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff_ms=2000, retry_on=[network_timeout, 429, 503, 502] — rationale: minimize duplicate side-effects while allowing one automatic retry for transient transport issues.
  - balanced_read (for query/embeddings/generation where retries yield clear user value): max_attempts=4, initial_backoff_ms=100, multiplier=1.6, max_backoff_ms=3000, retry_on=[network_timeout, 408, 429, 500, 502, 503] — rationale: more aggressive to prioritize availability/latency for read-like operations.
  - background_queued (non-latency-blocking background tasks): max_attempts=8, initial_backoff_ms=200, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff_ms=15000, retry_on=[all_transient]

- Jitter strategy: full jitter for all templates (draw uniform(0, backoff) to avoid synchronized thundering).

Idempotency key contract:
- Header: Idempotency-Key (case-insensitive) recommended for HTTP; for gRPC use metadata key "idempotency-key".
- Who may generate: client should supply for any mutation operation. SDKs will auto-generate a UUIDv4 when convenience helpers (e.g., create_resource_retryable()) are used unless the caller explicitly passes a key. Auto-key generation will be opt-in via a helper flag (auto_idempotency=true) to avoid accidental duplicates for very sensitive ops.
- TTL and scope: server-side keys are expected to be valid for 24 hours; SDKs should annotate keys with operation intent via optional header Idempotency-Semantics: "mutation|retryable-read" to help server logging.
- Streaming writes: idempotency scope combines session-id + sequence-window. For streaming operations that can be resumed, clients MUST include a stable session identifier (client-generated UUID) as Idempotency-Key and attach sequence numbers in payload envelopes; SDKs will expose StreamResumeManager to manage this pattern.

Retryable error taxonomy (client-side):
- transient_transport: network socket errors, DNS failures, TLS handshake timeouts, request canceled by client. Retryable with conservative limits.
- throttling: HTTP 429 and explicit server throttle headers; should respect Retry-After when provided; otherwise use capped backoff.
- transient_service: 502, 503, 504, some 500s flagged with X-Transient: true by server. Retryable for read/balanced policies; mutation behavior depends on idempotency.
- client_error_no_retry: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (conflict), 422 — do not retry by default.
- fatal_server_error: 501, 505 — do not retry and surface immediately.

Mapping rules (examples):
- 429 -> throttling. If Retry-After present: respect header and escalate to max_backoff_ms if necessary.
- 503 -> transient_service. If response contains Retry-After or X-Transient: false, follow factors accordingly.
- 409 -> client_error_no_retry for mutations unless server explicitly documents safe retries for that endpoint.

Streaming-specific ergonomics:
- Checkpoint cadence: SDKs should checkpoint resume token every ~1k tokens OR every 5s (whichever comes first) for long-running streams to bound replay/dedup windows.
- Deduplication window: recommend servers perform dedup by token-range idempotency with a conservative 5s/50-token window; SDKs should avoid re-sending already-acknowledged frames and maintain a small local ledger for in-flight messages.
- Resume semantics: client stores the last acked sequence id locally and sends Resume-Token header; if Resume-Token unknown, fall back to full replay. SDKs will expose a StreamResumeManager that persists resume metadata to a pluggable storage adapter (default: in-memory ephemeral with optional file-backed/OS keychain adapter).

Telemetry & safeguards:
- SDKs must emit metrics: retries_per_op, idempotency_key_used (yes/no), resumed_streams_count, duplicate_responses_detected.
- When auto-idempotency is used for a mutation, SDK emits a warning event to logs and telemetry (so customers can audit).

Docs & migration:
- Provide a migration guide that:
  1) explains difference between auto-generated keys and explicit keys;
  2) how to choose conservative_mutation vs balanced_read;
  3) patterns for idempotent server design and server headers to make endpoints safely retryable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cross-lang spec doc reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go).
- 3 example client snippets (Python, TypeScript, Go) showing: 1) explicit idempotency-key write with conservative_mutation; 2) auto-idempotency helper with explicit opt-in; 3) streaming resume using StreamResumeManager.
- Unit tests: per-language retry policy unit tests + e2e canary asserting no duplicates for a simulated flaky server.
- Console and metrics: dashboards capture retries_per_op and duplicates > 0 will open an alert.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: finalize cross-lang spec and agree primitive names.
- Week 2: implement templates in each SDK + tests.
- Week 3: docs + migration guide + sample apps.
- Week 4: publish and monitor canary + iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-lang spec signed off by SDK leads (Python, TS, Go)
3 example snippets: explicit idempotency write, auto-idempotency helper, streaming resume
Unit tests for each retry template and mapping rules
E2E canary demonstrating no duplicate side-effects under simulated network flakiness
design_decisions: Use small set of opinionated templates instead of per-endpoint heuristics to simplify developer mental model
Full jitter for all backoffs to avoid synchronized retries
Require explicit opt-in for auto-generated idempotency keys on mutation helpers to reduce accidental duplicates
Expose StreamResumeManager as a pluggable component so platforms can persist resume metadata in a customer-chosen storage
implementation_notes: SDK API surface: RetryPolicy (builder), IdempotencyScope helper, StreamResumeManager with default in-memory and optional file adapter
Telemetry: implement SDK-level counters and events for retries_per_op and idempotency_key_warning
Docs: confluence draft at the provided link and quickstart snippets for each language
